p. as feature of beauty, ע ׳יְפֵה‎ Deut 16:12; compare Song 4:9; 7:5, ׳ע יוֺנִים‎ 1:15; 4:1; and 5:12 (כְּיוֺנִים‎); on other hand, ׳ע רַכּוֺת לֵאָה‎ Gen 29:17 (E); ע בַּמּוּךְ ׳וַתָּשֶׂם‎ 2Kin 9:30 (see מּוּךְ‎), compare Jer 4:30, ע ׳כָּחַל‎ Ezek 23:40 paint the eyes .

q. apple of the eye, see אִישׁוֺן‎, [בָּבָה‎], בַּת‎

r. ע ׳גַּבֹּת‎ Lev 14:9 eyebrows.

s. מִָיּ֑יִן ע ׳חַכְלִילִי‎ Gen 49:12, ע ׳חַכְלִילוּת‎ Prov 23:29 (see ׳ח‎); ע ׳מְאוֺר‎ 15:30, see Toy.

2. a. eyes as shewing mental qualities: arrogance ׳ע גַבְהוּת‎ Isa 2:11, ׳ע גְבֹהִים‎ 5:15, ׳גְּבַהּעֿ‎ Psa 101:5, ע רוּם ׳תִּפְאֶרֶת‎ Isa 10:12; with רוּם‎ also Psa 18:28 (so read also || 2Sam 22:28 Hup HPS), 2Sam 131:1; Prov 6:17; 21:4; humility, ע ׳שַׁח‎ Job 22:29; mockery, ׳ע לְ תִּלְעַג‎ Prov 30:17; compare ע ׳רָעָה בְּ‎ Deut 15:9 (grudging), 28:54, 56 (id.); especially (עַל‎) ׳ע אַלתָּֿחֹס‎ not have pity on 7:16 4t. Deuteronomy; Ezek 5:11 8t. Ezekiel; Isa 13:18, also Gen 45:20 (E; = not regret); compare מֵע יִסָּתֵר ׳נֹחַם‎ Hosea 13:14.

b. ע ׳מַחְמַד‎ Ezek 24:16 desire of the eyes, so 24:21; 24:25; ע ׳שִׁקּוּצֵי‎ 20:7 abominations of the eyes, so 20:8. — Psa 73:7 see חֵלֶב‎.

3 Figurative of mental and spiritual faculties, acts and states:

a. ע ׳תִּמָּקַחְנָה‎ Gen 3:5, 7 (J) Isa 42:7, ע ׳גְּלּוּי‎ Num 24:4, 16 (JE); also ע מֵרְאוֺת ׳טַח‎ Isa 44:18; ׳ע ׳אֶליֿ‎ Psa 123:2 (see 123:2; 123:2 for origin of figurative), +; of ׳י‎, 33:18 (i.e. his favour) 34:16 (id. +.

b. ׳ע הַזִּנוֺת‎ Ezek 6:9; ע ׳תִּשְׂבַּע‎ Eccl 1:8; 4:8; ע ׳שָֽׁאֲלוּ‎ 2:10; ׳ע יַבִּיטוּ לְֹנכַח‎ Prov 4:25; ׳טוֺבעֿ‎ 22:9 = bountiful, עָ֑יִן רַע‎ 23:6 = niggardly one, so 28:22; eye as avenue of temptation Job 31:1, 7; ע ׳שִׁית‎ Psa 17:11 +?

c. especially בְּעֵינֵי‎, with adjective and intransitive verbs, in the view, opinion, of Gen 16:4-5, (J), 21:11-12, (E), 34:18 (P), + often; with active verb 2Sam 10:3 = 1Chr 19:3; Est 1:17; 3:6; בְּע ׳הַטּוֺב‎ Gen 16:6; 19:14 (J), +, i.e. what one pleases, Num 36:6 (P) whom they please; בְּע ׳הַיָּשָׁר‎ Deut 12:8, 25 +, בְּע וְהַיָּשָׁר ׳הַטּוֺב‎ 12:28; Josh 9:25 (D), בְּע ׳הָרַע‎ Judg 2:11; 3:7; Deut 4:25 + especially D and Kings (RD); so עיניו לְנֶגֶד‎ 2Sam 22:25 = Psa 18:25; עֵינֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵי‎ Num 15:39 = according to your wish, fancy (+ לְבַבְכֶם‎).

d. מֵע ׳נֶעְלָם‎ Lev 4:13 i.e. hid from knowledge of, so Num 5:13 (both P), Job 28:21; ׳מֵע‎ Num 15:24 (P) without the knowledge of; ע ׳אַעְלִים מִן‎ Isa 1:15 = disregard, pay no attention; compare Lev 20:4 (H) Ezek 22:26; without מִן‎, absolute, Prov 28:27; מֵע ׳נִסְתְּרוּ‎ Isa 65:16, מֵע עָמָל ׳וַיַּסְתֵּר‎ Job 3:10; ע ׳אַעְלִים בּוֺ‎ (i.e. בַּכֹּפֶר‎) 1Sam 12:3 (נעלים‎ sandals + ᵐ5 בי ענו‎ Th We Kit, compare Ecclusxlvi. 19; Bu HPS insert בי ענו‎); ע יְעַוֵּר ׳הַשֹּׁחַד‎ Deut 16:19, compare ע ׳כְּסוּת‎ Gen 20:16 (E).

4 Transferred meanings:

a. visible surface of earth Exod 10:5, 15 (J) Num 22:5, 11 (JE).

b. appearance Lev 13:5 (P; reading בְּעֵינוֺ‎ Di Kau Dr-Wh), 13:37 (P; reading id.), 13:55 (P) Num 11:7 (twice in verse) (JE); so apparently dual 1Sam 16:7.

c. gleam, sparkle (of metal, jewels, etc.) Ezek 1:4, 7, 16, 22, 27; 8:2; 10:9; Dan 10:6; of wine Prov 23:31.

5 Other phrases are: ׳ע ע ׳תַּחַת‎ Exod 21:24 (E) = Lev 24:20 (H), = ׳ע ׳בְּע‎ Deut 19:21, all = an eye for an eye; ׳ע ׳בְּע‎ = eye to eye, Num 14:14 (P) Isa 52:8 (figurative), compare ׳וְע ׳אֶתעֿ תִּרְאֶינָה‎ Jer 32:4; 34:3; especially לְעֵינֵי‎ in the presence of, in full view of Gen 42:24 (E) 47:19 (J) Exod 4:30 (J) Num 19:5 (P), + oft; of business transaction Jer 32:12 (twice in verse); Gen 23:11, 18 (P); so ע ׳נֶגֶד‎ Joel 1:16, ע ׳לְנֶגֶד‎ Job 4:16, and even ׳בְּע‎ 1Sam 21:14; Ezra 3:12; ע מִנֶּגֶד ׳נִגְרַזְתּי‎ Psa 31:23; ע ׳בֵּין‎ = on the forehead Exod 13:9, 16 (JE) Deut 6:8; 11:18; 14:1; Dan 8:5, 21.

II. עַ֫יִן‎ noun feminine spring (of water) (connection with I. ׳ע‎ dubious; Late Hebrew id., Phoenician ען‎; Assyrian ênu, înu; Arabic ; Ethiopic ; Palmyrene עַיְינָא עֵינָא, ᵑ7 עינא,‎; Syriac ); — absolute ׳ע‎ 1Sam 29:1 +, עָ֑יִן‎ Gen 49:22 +, הָעַ֫יְנָה‎ 24:16, 45; construct עֵין‎ 24:13 +; plural עֲיָנֹת‎ Deut 8:7, וֺת‎-2Chr 32:3; construct עֵינוֺת‎ Exod 15:27 = Num 33:9, עִינוֺת‎ Prov 8:28 (Ges§ 93v); — spring Gen 16:7; 24:16, 29, 30, 42, 45 (all J) 49:22 (poem in J), 1Sam 29:1; חַמַּיִם עֵין‎ Gen 16:7; 24:13, 43 (J), compare Exod 15:27 (J) Num 33:9 (P); וּתְחֹמֹת ע מַיִם ׳נַחֲלֵי‎ Deut 8:7; הָעֲיָנוֺת מֵימֵי‎2Chr 32:3; ׳ְ תְּהוֺם‎ Prov 8:28 (i.e. of the sea); figurative יַעֲקֹב עֵין‎ Deut 33:28 (poem), i.e. Jacob's descendants. Particular springs are:

a. ׳ע חֲרֹד‎ Judg 7:1 (on location compare GFM).

b. ׳ע הַקּוֺרֵא‎ (partridge-spring) Judg 15:19 (compare id.).

c. ׳ע רֹגֵּל‎ near Jerusalem (early sanctuary RSSem i. 157, 2nd ed. 172) 2Sam 17:17 compare 1Kin 1:2, on border of Judah Josh 15:7, and Benjamin 18:16.

d. ׳ע הַתַּנִּין‎ (dragon-spring) Neh 2:13 (= c ? so RSl.c.). — On הָעַיִן שַׁעַר‎ 2:14; 3:15; 12:37 see שַׁעַר‎

[עַ֫יִן‎] noun feminineEzra 5:5 eye (see Biblical Hebrew I. ׳ע‎); — construct עֵין‎ 5:5 (of God); plural (K§ 51, 1) of horn, עַיְנִין‎ Dan 7:8, 20; of man, dual construct עַיְנֵי‎ 7:8, suffix עַיְנַי‎ 4:31.

כמהן.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

כמו.def:
H3644. kemo

or kamo כְּמוֺ‎ adverb and

conjunction like, as, when (literally the like of what (namely) . . ., a pleonastic form of כְּ‎ (see מוֺ‎), and, like it, properly a substantive: compare Aramaic כְּמָא‎ like Psa 78:68 Levy, usually דְּ כְּמָא‎ like as; (i.e. ) like what, like, usually followed by like as; Samaritan ; Arabic Ethiopic kama, like as, Di Gr§ 63 a Sabean כמו‎ZMG 1883, 394) — used

1 (56 t.) as an independent word (except Gen 19:15; Neh 9:11, only in poetry);

2 as an equivalent for כְּ‎ before suffixes, always before light ones, and occasionally before heavy ones (see כְּ‎ at the beginning): —

1. a. adverb, as poetic synonym of כְּ‎, like, as, Exod 15:5 they went down כמואֿבן‎ like a stone (hence in prose Neh 9:11), 9:8 (Psa 78:13), Isa 30:22; 51:6 (see כֵּן‎), 26:17 לָלֶרֶת תַּקְרִיב חָרָח כְּמוֺ‎ (see כְּ‎ 1c (2), on the construct: so 41:25; Psa 58:5, 8a,9), Isa 26:18 we have brought forth the like of, as it were, wind, Jer 13:21; 15:18; 50:26; Ezek 16:57 (עת כמו‎ as at the time of: see כְּ‎ Note), Hosea 7:4; 8:12; 13:7; Hab 3:14 (as it were), Zech 9:15; 10:2, 7 (as with wine: see ib.) Elsewhere chiefly in Psalms (19 t.) and Job (11 t.), as Psa 29:6; 61:7; 63:6; 78:69; 79:5; 88:6; 90:9; Job 6:15; 10:22 (twice in verse); 12:3 אלה כמו‎ the like of these things, 14:9; Song 6:10; 7:2; Lam 4:6 רגע כמו‎ (in prose כרגע‎). Repeated, like כְּ ֗֗֗ כְּ‎, Psa 58:10; and answered by כֵּן‎ Isa 26:17. — Psa 58:8b יתמוללו כמו‎, as it were is against usage of כמו‎ (with a verb), and yields a lame sense: read perhaps ׳ית‎ [חָצִיר‎] כמו‎ (Lag Che); 73:15 if I said, כְמ֑וֺ אֲסַמְּרָה‎, the text is untranslateable, the rendering thus for כמו‎ being indefensible: probably הֵנָּה‎ has dropped out before the following ׃הִנֵּה‎ for הֵנָּה כְּמוֺ‎ the like of these things, compare Job 23:14 כָּהֵנָּה‎, and 12:3 above

b. conjunction = כַּאֲשֶׁר‎: (a) of time, once, Gen 19:15 הַשַּׁחַר עָלָה כְּמוֺ‎ when the dawn arose; (β) of mode, according as, Zech 10:8 רָבוּ כְּמוֺ וְרָבוּ‎ Prov 23:7 (answered by כֵּן‎). — For

2 (before suffixes), see עכּ‎.

כמוש.def:
H3645. Kemosh

or Kemish כְּמוֺשׁ‎ proper name, of a divinity Chemosh (כמש‎ MI3. 5. 9. 12. 13. 14. 18. 19. 32. 23 also כמש עשתר‎ Jer 1:17 and proper name, masculine כמשמלך‎ 1:1; Assyrian Kammusunadbi, a king of Moab SchrCOT i, 281; = KAT2, 288; compare further BaeRel 13 f. 238, 256 NöZMG 1888, 471; ᵐ5‎ Ξαμώς); — god of the Moabites to whom Solomon erected a high place 1Kin 11:7, 33; 2Kin 23:13; Jer 48:7 (Kt כמישׁ‎), 48:13. Moab is ׳עַםכֿ‎ Num 21:29 (ode) people of Chemosh, and Moabites his sons and daughters, compare Jer 48:46. He is said to be also the God of the Ammonites Judg 11:25 (probably an error BaeRel 15 GFM).

כמז‎ (√ of following; meaning dubious; Arabic is bunch, heap).

כמישׁ‎ Jer 48:7 Kt, see כְּמוֺשׁ‎. above

כמן‎ (√ of following (si vera l); perhaps be hidden; compare Aramaic כְּמַן‎, , lie in ambush; Arabic id. is denominative from loan-word according to Frä243).

כמן.def:
H3646. kammon

כַּמֹּן‎ noun masculine cummin, plant grown as condiment (ᵐ5‎ κύμινον, cuminum cyminum; Plin.NH xix. 8; German 'römischer Kümmel;' LöwNo. 152; √ dubious; Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic כַּמּוֺנָא‎, ; Arabic , Ethiopic on formative compare LagBN 89; loan-word according to Di832); — Isa 28:25, 27 (twice in verse).

כמס.def:
H3647. kamas

[כָּמַס‎] verb store up (si vera 1.), in

Qal Passive participle כָּמֻס‎ Deut 32:34 is not this stored up (laid up in store) with me (|| בְּאוֺצְרֹתָ֑י חָתוּם‎); but read probably כָנֻס‎ in same. meaning (see כנס‎, and Dr32:34).

כמר.def:
H3649. komer

[כֹּ֫מֶר‎] noun masculine (idol-)priest (so Late Hebrew כּוּמָר‎; Aramaic , כּוּמְרָא‎, is also priest of God; Nerab כמר‎ HalRev. Semitic 1896, 280, 282; Nabataean כמר‎ priest CISii, No. 170, Teima כמרא‎ id. CISii, No. 113 a, b, b bis; so כמר‎ Neo-Punic EutZMG. 1875, 238, 239 BergerJAs Apr.-June, 1887, 465; perhaps Tel Amarna kamiru BezBM.:Tabl, xxvi; Or. Dipl. 92; WklTA. 1, 15, 33 leaves untranslated); — plural absolute, in O.T. only of idol-priests; הַכְּמָרִים‎ 2Kin 23:5, כְּמָרָיו‎ Hosea 10:5, ׳הַכּ עִםהַֿכֹּהֲנִים‎ Zeph 1:4. In Hosea 4:4 Beck (in Wü142) We proposes כִּכְמָרָיו וְעַמִּי‎ (for כִּמְרִיבֵי וְעַמְּךָ ᵑ0‎).

כמת‎ (√ of following, meaning unknown).

כמריר.def:
H3650. kimrir

[כִּמְרִיר‎] noun masculine darkness, gloominess (?), plural intensive construct יוֺם כִּמְרִירֵי‎ Job 3:5 the deep gloom of day (|| עֲנָנָה צלמות, חשֶׁךְ,‎); — read ׳כַּמ‎, see Di Sta§ 231.

III. כמר‎ (√ of following; compare Assyrian kamâru, overthrow, lay prostrate, whence noun kamâru, net, snare DlHWB 336 and כֹּמֶר‎ priest according to DlHA 42, i.e. one who prostrates himself; also Mandean כמר‎ turn round, bring back NöM 443 f. and North Syriac pursue Nöib PS1759).

כן.def:
H3651. ken

I. כֵּן‎ adjective right, veritable, honest (properly firm, upright; Syriac recte PS1662) — absolute כֵּן‎ Exod 10:29 + (on possibly construct see

2 near the end); plural כֵּנִים‎ Gen 42:11, 19, 31, 33, 34; —

1 right, usually indecl., often as substantive a right thing, especially with vbb. dicendi Exod 10:29 (J) דִּבַּרְתָּ כֵּן‎, Num 27:7 דֹּבְרֹת כֵּן‎, 36:5 (both P); יַאֲרִיךְ כֵּן‎ Prov 28:2 (the) right (i.e. order and justice) shall last long (see De Now VB); = adverb aright, of pronunciation Judg 12:6; also with verb agendi Eccl 8:10 (on Isa 33:23 see III. כֵּן‎ below כנן‎); right well Psa 65:10; (Che; al. = so); with לֹא‎, as adjective, not right לֹאכֵֿן אֲשֶׁר דְּבָרִים‎ 2Kin 17:9 things which were not right (verb agendi); of heart of a fool Prov 15:7; Jer 23:10; as substantive = what is not right, upright 8:6; with verb agendi לֹאכֵֿן‎ 2Kin 7:9 that which is not right we are doing, Jer 48:30 b.

2 veritable, true, כֵּןצְֿדָקָה‎ Prov 11:19 the veritable of righteousness = true righteousness; Isa 16:6 = Jer 48:30 a may be either their boastings are not true or (Thes Che Di Du Gr Gie and others) the untruth of their boastings (לֹאכֵֿן‎ as compound construct); absolute, in assent to something already said, Right! Correct! True! Josh 2:4.

3 plural concrete honest (men) Gen 42:11, 19, 31, 33, 34 (all E). — II. כֵּן‎ thus, so, see below; III. כֵּן‎ place, base, see below כנן‎; IV. [כֵּן‎], כִּנָּם כִּנִּם,‎, see below כנן‎.

I. כֵּן‎ adverb so (PH. Late Hebrew ᵑ7‎ id.; Syriac is then, Arabic , , but: probably from the demonstrative √ ka, found in כִּי‎ etc., Köii. 1, 254); (הִיא‎) כֶּןהֿוּא‎ Gen 44:10 4t.: — so (i.e. usually, as has been described or commanded, with reference to what has preceded), mostly of manner, but sometimes also of quantity, quality, or degree:

1. a. Judg 5:31 יאבדו כן‎ so perish thy enemies, Job 5:27 הִיאכֶּןֿ‎, 8:13 אל שׁכחי כל ארחות כן‎, Prov 6:29; 8:13; 2Sam 16:23; Isa 36:6; 47:15 לך היו כן‎, Num 13:33 בעיניהם היינו וכן‎; 9:16 תמיד יהיה כָן‎ Exod 10:14 (twice in verse) וג ארבה׳כמהו כן היה לא‎ (i. e. in such numbers), 1Kin 10:12 בא לא אלמגים עצי כן‎, 10:20; 2Chr 1:12 (twice in verse), Judg 21:14 מצאו כןולא להם‎ and they did not suffice for them so (namely in such numbers of them as there were); 1Kin 6:26 השׁני הכרוב וכן‎, Ezek 41:7; ל ׳וכן‎ Exod 27:11; 1Kin 10:29; Ezek 40:16; 2Chr 35:12, compare 1Chr 23:30; ל ׳כן‎ Exod 25:33 (compare 26:24), Josh 21:40.

b. the force of כֵּן‎ has sometimes to be elicited from the context : 1Kin 2:7 אלי קרבו כן כי‎ (that is, with kindness such as that enjoined in va), 20:40 משׁפטך כן‎, Jer 14:10 אהבו לנועכן‎ (i.e. not less than ׳י‎ has withdrawn from them 14:9, Gf Ke; Gie proposes אָכֵן‎), Psalm 61:9 אֲזַמְּרָה שִׁמְךָכֵּן‎ (Hi כְּצִדְקְךָ‎, implied in 14:6-8), Psa 63:3 בַּקֹּדֶשׁ חֲזִיתִךָכֵּן‎ (that is, with the longings of 63:2), 63:5 בְחַיָּיכֵּן אֲבָרֶכְךָ‎ (that is חַסְדְּךָ כְּרֹב‎ 63:4), 65:10 תְּכִינֶהָ כֵן כִּי‎ (i.e. so Generously, 65:10), 90:12 הוֺדַע כֵּן יָמֵינוּ לִמְנוֺת‎ (Hi י ׳כְּיִרְאַת‎ 90:11), 127:2 שֵׁנָא לִידִידוֺ יִתֵּן כֵּן‎ (that is, as abundantly; but Che אָכֵן‎), Prov 24:14 (see 24:13), Isa 52:14 מַרְאֵהוּ מֵאִישׁ מִשְׁחַת כֵּן‎ (sufficiently to justify רבים עליך שׁממו‎).

c. כן‎ occurs frequently in particular phrases, as (a) with הָיָה‎, especially כן ויהי‎ and it was so Gen 1:7, 9, 11 +, 2Kin 2:10 if thou seest me taken from thee כן יהילֿך‎ let it be to thee so (that is, as thou desirest), 7:20, with עשׂה‎ (especially וַיַּעֲשׂוּ וַיַּעַשׂ,‎) Gen 29:28; 42:20; 45:21 + often, Judg 7:16 תִּרְאוּ תַּעֲשׂוּמִמֶּנִּי וְכֵן‎, + ׳ל‎ Gen 42:25 כן להם ויעשׂ‎, Exod 22:29; 23:11 ל תעשׂה ׳כן‎, Deut 22:3; 2Sam 12:31; 1Kin 11:8 (compare 6:33; 7:18); Gen 29:26 במקומנו כן יֵעָשֶׂה לא‎, 34:7; 2Sam 13:12; rarer usages, כֵּן דִּבֶּר‎ Exod 6:9, כן אמר‎ 1Kin 22:8, אמרתם כֵּן‎ Ezek 11:5; 33:10, י יאֹמַר כֵּן ׳אָמֵן‎ 1Kin 1:36 (compare Jer 28:6), כֵּן יֹדֵעַ אבי שׁאול וגם‎ 1Sam 23:17; כֵּן אָהֵב‎ (idiomatic) to love (it) so, Jer 5:31; Amos 4:5; (b) Gen 50:3 כן כי החנֻטים ימי ימלאו‎ (compare Judg 14:10; 2Sam 13:18; Est 2:12); (c) alone, כֵּן אִם‎ if it be so Gen 25:22; 43:11; כִּיכֵֿןוַיִּרְאוּ‎ 1Sam 5:7, כִּיכֵֿן יָדַעְתִּי‎ Job 9:2; (d) כן לא‎ not so (namely as has been described or implied), with a substantive Num 12:7 משׁה עבדי כן לא‎, 2Sam 20:21; 23:5; Psa 1:4; Job 9:35b עמדי אנכי כילֿאכֿן‎ not so am I with myself (i.e. I am not conscious of being one who would fear him, va), with a verb Deut 18:14 י לך נתן כן ׳לא ואתה‎ (not so, — namely as implied in va), 2Sam 18:14; Isa 10:7 יחשׁב כן לא יְדַמֶּה, כן לא‎, absolute Gen 48:18 אבי כן לא‎, Exod 10:11.

2 Often, to emphasize the agreement, in answer to כְּ‎, and כַּאֲשֶׁר‎: namely

a. כֵּן ֗֗֗ כְּ‎, (a) Gen 44:10 = Josh 2:21 כֶּןהֿוּא כדבריכם‎ according to your words, so be it, 1Sam 25:25 כֶּןהֿוּא כשׁמו כי‎, Psa 48:11; Prov 23:7 כֶּןהֿוּא‎ (after conjunction כְּמוֺ‎), Ezek 42:11 רָחְבָּן כֵּן כְּאָרְכָּן‎; (b) Lev 27:12 יִהְיֶה כֵּן כְּעֶרְכְּךָ‎, 2Sam 13:35; Num 8:4; 9:14; 15:20; Deut 8:20; Judg 11:10, so after כְּפִי‎ Num 6:21; (c) ֗֗֗ כֵּן ֗֗֗ כְּכֹל‎ 1Sam 8:8; 2Sam 7:17; Jer 42:5; (d) in similes, (a) 2Sam 14:17 הא המלךכמלאך ׳אדני כן‎, Jer 18:6; Psa 123:2; 127:4; Prov 10:26; 26:8, 19; 27:8, 19; Song 2:2-3, (β) Joel 2:4 יְרוּצוּן כֵּן כְּפָרָשִׁים‎, Isa 31:5; 38:14; Psa 103:15; Prov 26:1-2, (γ) Psa 42:2 וג כן׳נפשׁי ֗֗֗ תערג כאיל‎ like the hind which etc., 83:16; Isa 61:11; 63:14; Job 7:3, so after כמו‎ Isa 26:17; (δ) Jer 2:26 הוֺבִישׁוּכְּבשֶׁת כֵּן ֗֗֗ גַּנָּב‎, 6:7; 34:5 (read כְּמשׂרפות‎), Ezek 22:22 (compare 22:20), 23:44; 34:12; compare (of degree) 35:15 (omitted by ᵐ5‎ Co), Hosea 4:7 לִי חָָֽטְאוּ כֵּן כְּרֻבָּם‎. Of time (un-common) 1Sam 9:13 אֹתוֺ תִּמְצְאוּן כֵּן הָעִיר כְּבֹאֲכֶם‎.

b. Ezra 10:12 לעשׂות עלינו כדבריך כן‎.

c. כַּאֲשֶׁר ֗֗֗ כֵּן ֗֗֗‎, (a) Exod 7:6 י צוה ׳כאשׁר עשׂו כן‎, 12:28, 50; 39:43 (compare 27:8), Num 8:22 (compare 5:4), Numbers 17:26; 36:10; Josh 14:5 (all P); Gen 41:13 היה כן פתר כאשׁר‎, Josh 10:1, 39; 11:15; Judg 1:7; 15:11b Psa 48:9; (b) (frequently) Num 2:17 יַחֲנוּ יִסָּ֑עוּכאשׁר כֵּן‎, Exod 1:12 (of degree = the more . . . the more) יִפְרֹץ וְכֵן יִרְבֶּה כֵּן אֹתוֺ יְעַנּוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר‎; (c) Gen 6:22 עשׂהככל כן אלהים אתו צוה אשׁר‎, Exod 39:32, 42; 40:16; Num 1:54; 2:34; 8:20; 9:5 (all P), compare Exod 25:9 (וְכֵן‎), simil. 2Sam 9:11; 2Kin 16:11, compare Josh 1:17; Jer 42:20; (d) Exod 27:8 יעשׂוכאשׁר כן אתך הֶרְאָה‎, 2Sam 16:19; 1Kin 2:38; Isa 20:4; 52:14f.; with the same verb repeated Lev 24:19-20, Deut 28:63 ישׂישׂ כן ֗֗֗ שׂשׂ כאשׁר‎, Josh 23:15; 1Sam 15:33; 26:24; 1Kin 1:37; Isa 10:11; Jer 5:19; 31:28; 32:42; 42:18; Ezek 12:11; 20:36; Zech 7:13; Prov 24:29; Num 14:28 כן דברתם כאשׁר לא אעשׂהאם‎, Isa 14:24, so after הלא‎ 10:11, after asseverative כי‎ 2Sam 3:9; 1Kin 1:30; so שֶׁ ׳כָּלעֻֿמַּת כֵּן ֗֗֗‎ Eccl 5:15; (e) Judg 7:17b תעשׂון כן אעשׂה כאשׁר‎, Lev 27:14; Num 15:14, compare Jer 39:12; (f) in similes, Deut 12:22; 22:26; Amos 3:12; Isa 65:8; Jer 13:11.

d. ֗֗֗ כאשׁר כן‎, (a) Exod 7:10 י צוה כאשׁר כן ׳ויעשׂו‎, 7:20; Josh 4:8; 2Sam 5:25; Ezek 12:7, compare Gen 50:12; Num 8:3; iron. Amos 5:14 י כן יהי ׳אמרתם כאשׁר אתּכם‎, Exod 10:10; (b) Gen 18:5 דברת כאשׁר תעשׂה כן‎, Neh 5:12. — Occasionally in poetry כאשׁר‎ is not expressed : Isa 54:9 (De), 55:9; Jer 3:20; Job 7:9; Hosea 11:2 מפניהם הלכו כן להם קראו‎ (of degree: so = in the same proportion), Psa 48:6 תמהו כן ראו המה‎ (i.e. in the same measure that they saw); Jer 33:22 (according to many, but dubious; read probably כאשׁר‎ Gie) it is represented by אשׁר‎ (so Isa 54:9 Hi Ew Di): Judg 5:15 כ‎ is not expressed. — Nahum 1:12 is probably corrupt; Zech 11:11 for עניי כן‎ read כְּנַעֲנֵי‎. — כָּזֹאת כָּכָה, כֹּה,‎ are synonyms, but differ considerably in usage.

3 With prepositions: —

a. מֵאַחֲרֵיכֵֿן אַחֲרֵיכֵֿן, אַחַרכֵּֿן,‎, literally after so, i.e. afterwards: see אַחַר‎.

b. בְּכֵן‎ (late), literally in such circumstances, i.e. thereupon, then, Eccl 8:10; Est 4:16 (בְּכֵין ᵑ7‎ often for אָז‎; e.g. Exod 15:1; SyrJerusalem = τότε).

c. כֵּןכְּמוֺֿ‎ Isa 51:6, according to some, like so, i.e. (Vrss Rabb) in like manner, or (De) like this (accompanied by a contemptuous gesture) = like a mere nothing: but see IV. כֵּן‎.

d. לָכֵן‎200 according to such conditions, that being so, therefore Num 16:11; 1Sam 27:6; Psa 16:9; 73:6; 73:10; especially in prophets, where it often introduces, after statement of the grounds, a divine declaration or command: Judg 10:13; 2Kin 1:6; Amos 4:12; Isa 5:13-14, 24; 7:14; 10:16; 16:7; 27:9; Jer 6:15; 8:10 etc.; י אמר כה ׳לכן‎ 2Kin 21:12; Isa 10:24; 28:16; 29:22; 30:12; 37:33; Jer 5:14; 6:21 + often; followed by האדון נאם‎ Isa 1:24; י ׳נאם‎ 1Sam 2:30; Jer 2:9; י נאם באים ימים הנה ׳לכן‎ 7:32; 16:14; 19:6 +; י נאם אני חי ׳לכן‎ Ezek 5:11; 35:6, 11; Zeph 2:9; לכן ֗֗֗ הנני‎ 1Kin 14:10; Hosea 2:8; 2:16; Isa 29:14; Jer 16:21; Ezek 16:37; 22:19; b 25:4, 7, 9 +; אֱמֹר לכן‎ Exod 6:6; Num 25:12 (both P), Ezek 11:16-17, 14:6; 20:30; 33:25; 36:22; דַּבֵּר לָכֵן‎ 14:4; 20:27; הִנָּכֵא לָכֵן‎ 11:4; 36:3, 6; 37:12; 38:14; . . . . שִׁמְעוּ לָכֵן‎ Isa 28:14; 51:21; Jer 6:18; 44:26 +. In answer to יען‎, Num 20:12 (P), 1Kin 14:10; 2Kin 1:16; 21:12; 22:20; Isa 29:14; 30:13; Jer 19:6 +, Ezek 5:8; 13:23 +; so, once, וְלָכֵן‎ Isa 8:7; to כי‎ 28:16; Jer 35:17; על‎ 9:14; אם‎ 23:38; 42:15. Special usages: — (a) idiomatic, in conversation, in reply to an objection, to state the ground upon which the answer is made; Gen 4:15 therefore — this being so — whoso killeth Cain, etc., 30:15; Judg 8:7; 11:8; 1Sam 28:2; 1Kin 22:19; Job 20:2 (ᵐ5‎ in Genesis Kings Job, not perceiving the idiom, renders οὐχοὕτως (as though לאכֿן‎): so also strangely, elsewhere, as 1Sam 3:14; 2Kin 1:4, 6; 21:12). (b) inferring the cause from the effect, or developing what is logically involved in a statement, Isa 26:14b (compare De) therefore thou hast visited and destroyed them (not a consequence of va 'the dead rise not,' but the development of what is implicit in it), 61:7; Jer 2:33; 5:2 (because namely אמונה אין‎ 5:1), Job 34:25; 42:3. — Zech 11:7 read הַצּאֹן לִכְנַעֲנֵי‎.

e. עַדכֵּֿן‎ hitherto (of time), as yet Neh 2:16.

f. עַלכֵּֿן‎145 upon ground of such conditions, therefore (introducing, more Generally than לָכֵן‎, the statement of a fact, rather than a declaration: never used in the phrases noted under לָכֵן‎), Gen 20:6; 42:21; Exod 5:8, 17; 16:29; 20:11; 1Sam 20:29; 28:18; 2Sam 7:22, 27; 1Kin 20:23; Isa 5:25; 9:16; 13:7, 13; 15:4, 7; 16:9, 11; 17:10; 21:3; Jer 5:6, 27; 10:21; 12:8; 20:11; 31:3, 20; Ezek 7:20; 22:4; 31:5 etc., Psa 1:5; 42:7; 45:3 c (the poet's inference from va. b), Psalm 1:8; 110:7; Job 6:3; 9:22; 17:4; 20:21 etc., Song 1:3; and regularly where the origin of a name, or custom, or proverb is assigned, Gen 2:24 וג אישׁ יעזב ׳עלכֿן‎, 10:9 יֵאָמַ֔רעלכֿן‎, 11:9 בבל שׁמה קרא עלכֿן‎, 16:14; 19:22; 21:31; 25:30; 26:33; 29:34; 29:35; 30:6; Genesis 32:33; 47:22; Exod 13:15; 15:23; Num 18:24; 21:14, 27; Deut 10:9 (compare 15:11, 15; 19:7; 24:18, 22), Josh 7:26; 14:14; Judg 15:19; 18:12; 1Sam 5:5; 10:12; 23:28 (? read so 27:6) 2Sam 5:8, 20 etc.; הַעַלכֵּֿן‎ Hab 1:17. — Est 9:26 the 2nd כן על‎ (unless dittograph) points unusually onwards to דברי כל האגרתעל‎ on this account, on account, namely, etc.

II. כֵּן‎ see כון‎; III. כֵּן‎ see I. כנן‎; IV. כֵּן‎ see II. כנן‎. p. 467, below

adverb thus, as follows (Biblical Hebrew כֵּן‎; כֵּן ᵑ7‎, Syriac ); — usually with אֲמַר‎ (אָמַ‎, etc.; compare Egyptian Aramaic CISii. 149 A 1, B-C 3 RÉS492B 5), Dan 2:24 אֲמַרלֵֿהּ וְכֵן‎, 2:25; 4:11; 6:7; 7:5, 23; Ezra 5:3; 6:2 בְּגַוַּהּ תִיב וְכֵןכְּֿ‎.

כנה.def:
ב‎

בּ ב,‎, Bêth, 2nd letter; post Biblical Hebrew = numeral 2 (and so in margin of printed MT); ב֟‎ = 2000; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

I. בְּ‎,

preposition in (Moabite בּ‎, Syriac , Arabic , Ethiopic ) before tone-syllables in certain cases (Ges§ 102. 2) בָּ‎, with suffix בִּי‎; בְּךָ‎ (Ex 7:29; 2Sam 22:30; Psa 141:8 בְּכָה‎), in pause and feminine בָּךְ‎; בּוֺ‎ (once, Jer 17:24 Kt בֹּה‎), בָּהּ‎; בָּנוּ‎; בָּכֶם‎, [בָּכֶן‎]; בָּם בָּהֶם,‎ [also בָּהֵ֫מָּה‎ Exod 30:4; 36:1; Hab 1:16], בָּהֶן‎ 1Sam 31:7; Isa 38:16; Ezek 42:14 [15 times בָּהֵן‎ (FrMM 235), and thrice, Leviticus 5:22; Num 13:19; Jer 5:17, בָּהֵ֫נָּה‎]. Preposition denoting properly in, Greek ἐν, but applied in many derived and figurative significations. The senses expressed by בְּ‎ are grouped by the Rabbis in three classes, הַכְּלִי בֵּית‎ Beth vasculi, וְהַנְּגִיעָה הַדִּיבִּוּק בֵּית‎ Beth coniunctionis et viciniae, הָעֵזֶר בֵּית‎ Beth auxilii; and the same arrangement may be followed here, though the limits between the three classes are not clearly defined, and they sometimes overlap one another.

I. In:

1 strictly, of position in a place (which often is expressed more precisely by בְּתוֺךְ בְּקֶרֶב,‎), as בַּבַּיִת‎ in the house, בָּעִיר‎ in the city, בַּדּוּד‎ in the pot, בָּאָרֶץ‎ in the land, etc. constantly. Hebrew idiom also says בָּהָר‎ in the mountain Exod 24:18 etc., even in cases where we could hardly avoid saying on, as 1Kin 11:7; 19:11: so בְּחֹרֵב‎ Deut 1:16 and elsewhere; הָהָר בְּראֹשׁ‎ Exod 24:17; Psa 72:16. Preceded by a verb of motion (especially עָבַר‎) בְּ‎ = through, as Gen 12:6 and Abram passed through בָּאָרֶץ‎ in the land = passed through it, 13:17; 2Sam 24:2 +; in (= through) a gate, Isa 62:10; Jer 17:19; Micah 2:13. Figurative to speak בְּאָזְנֵי‎ in the ears of ...; to be good (or evil, etc.) בְּעֵינֵי‎ in the eyes of ...

2 of presence in the midst of a multitude, among, Exod 14:28 there was not left בָּהֶם‎ among them even one, Lev 26:36; 2Sam 15:31 Ahitophel בַּקֹּשְׁרִים‎ is among the conspirators, 2Kin 18:5 יְהוּדָה מַלְכֵי בְּכֹל‎. So בְּךָ‎ in thee (of Israel, collective) Deut 7:14; 15:4, 7; 18:10; 23:11; 28:54 (different from עִמָּ֑ח‎ beside thee Lev 25:35). — Specifically

a. of an individual, implying eminency among: Josh 14:15; Jer 46:18 Tabor among the mountains, 49:15; Prov 30:30; Song 1:8 בַנָּשִׁים הַיָּפָה‎ the fair one (= the fairest) among women, Lam 1:1: compare Luke 1:42. On 1Sam 17:12 see Dr.

b. hence with some verbs, when the action refers to only a part of the object, as בְּ הִכָּהַ‎ to smite among... i.e. to smite some of... (different from הִכָּה‎ with accusative); בְּ הָרַג‎ Psa 78:31; בְּ נָשָׂא‎ to bear in, i.e. to share in bearing, Num 11:17 and elsewhere; בְּ בָּנָה‎ to build in or at Zech 6:15; Neh 4:4; בְּ עָשָׂה‎ Exod 5:9; בְּ עָמֵל‎ to labour on Jonah 4:10; בְּ שָׁתָה בְּ, אָכַל‎ to eat or drink of Judg 13:16; Prov 9:5; בְּ חָלַק‎ to give a share in Job 39:17.

c. specifying the parts of which a whole consists (especially in P) Gen 7:21; 8:17; 9:10, 16; 17:23; Exod 12:19; Num 31:11, 26; Hosea 4:3.

3 with reference to the limits enclosing a space, within: Exod 20:10 בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ‎ within thy gates, Isa 56:5 בְּחוֺמוֺתַי‎ within my walls.

4 often pregn. with verbs of motion, when the movement to a place results in rest in it, into: after בָּא‎ Gen 19:8; Isa 19:23; נָתַן‎ Gen 27:17; שָׁלַח‎ to send Lev 16:22; in among Josh 23:7, 12; 1Kin 11:2. — Hosea 12:7 (an extreme case) בְּ שׁוּב‎ to return (and rest) in thy God, 1Sam 16:3 (unless לַזָּבַ֑ח‎ should be read, as 16:7). — בְּעַיִן עַיִן‎ (with) eye (looking) into eye Num 14:14; Isa 52:8; בְּפָנִים מָּנִים‎ Deut 5:4; פְ ׳עֵינֵי בְּ‎ the eyes of ... are upon, both in favourable (11:12; Psa 101:6) and hostile (Amos 9:8; Job 7:8) sense.

5 applied to time, as Gen 1:1 בְּרֵאשִׁית‎ in the beginning; 2:2 הַשְּׁבִיעִי בַּיּוֺם‎ on the seventh day; Judg 10:8 הַהִיא בַּשָּׁנָה‎ in that year; & constantly.

6 of a state or condition, whether material or mental, in which an action takes place: so often, בְּשָׁלוֺם‎ in peace Gen 15:15; בַּצָּרָה‎ in distress Psa 91:15; בְּתֻמּוֺ הָלַךְ‎ to walk in his integrity; Exod 5:19 בְּרָע‎ in evil case.

7 בְּ‎ introduces the predicate, denoting it as that in which the subject consists, or in which it shews itself (the Beth essentiae, — common in Arabic, especially with a participle or adjective and in a negative sentence: Qor 2:79 and God (appears) not as one remiss; 2:7 and they are not believers [compare French en — en honnête homme]; see WAG ii. § 56 a): namely

a. a primary predicate, Exod 18:4 the God of my fathers בְּעֶזְרִי‎ was my help, Psa 146:5; Hosea 13:9 (read בְעֶזְֶרךָ׃ מִי כִּי‎ with ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Che and others); Psa 68:5 שְׁמוֺ בְּיָהּ‎ his name consists in Yah, Job 23:13; 37:10. With the predicate in the plural (as plural of majesty) Psa 118:7 ׳י בְּעֹזְרָ֑י‎ J. is my great helper, 54:6 (see Che), Judg 11:35.

b. a secondary predicate, Exod 6:3 and I appeared unto them שַׁדָּ֑י בְּאֵל‎ as God Almighty, Num 26:53 בְּנַחֲלָה‎ as an inheritance, 34:2; Ezek 46:16; 47:14; Deut 10:22; 26:14 I have not put away therefrom בְּטָמֵא‎ as one unclean = while unclean, 28:62; Isa 40:10 יָבוֺא בְּחָזָק‎ he cometh as a strong one, Psa 35:2 (where see De) and rise up as my help, 35:16, 39:7; 55:19; Prov 3:26; Job 36:32 (De).

c. a predicate as accusative, Isa 48:10 I have refined thee בְכָ֑סֶף וְלֹא‎ but not as though silver, Ezek 20:41; Num 18:26; 36:2; Josh 13:6-7, 23:4; Ezek 45:1; 47:22 (twice in verse) (read יַמִּלוּ‎) 48:29 (see ᵐ5‎ Co) all בְּנַחֲלָה‎ (compare

b.), Psa 78:55 & allotted it נַחֲלָה בְּחֶבֶל‎ as a line of inheritance (i.e. as a measured inheritance). Isa 26:4 י עוֺלָמִים צוּר יהוה בְּיָהּ ׳כִּי‎ is different — for in Yah there is a rock of ages (compare Qor 4:7; 4:47 there is sufficiency in God as a patron).

d. in comparisons, Psa 37:20 consume away בֶּעָשָׁן‎ in the form of, as, smoke 78:33; 102:4; Job 34:36; 36:14.

II. Denoting proximity —

1 at, by (not very common): 1Sam 29:1 בָּעַיִן‎ by the spring; Ezek 10:15, 20 כְּבָר בִּנְהַר‎ by the river Chebar (1:3 עַל‎).

2 on: Gen 8:20; Num 23:2 בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ‎ on the altar; Judg 8:21 on the necks of the camels; 1Kin 2:5 and elsewhere בְּמָתְנָיו‎ on his loins; Isa 59:17 a helmet בְּראֹשׁוֺ‎ on his head.

3 often with verbs of touching, approaching, taking hold of, cleaving, etc., as תָּפַשׂ תָּמַךְ, מָּגַּע, קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, נָגַע, חָשַׁק, דָּבֵק, אָחַז,‎ (see these words).

4 with words expressing or implying an act of hostility —

a. against: Gen 16:12 בּוֺ כֹּל וְיַד בַכֹּל יָדוֺ‎ his hand against all, and the hand of all against him; מְּ יַד ׳הָֽיְתָה בּ‎ Deut 13:10; 1Sam 5:9; 18:17 +? verbs (q. v.) of fighting (רִיב נִלְחַם,‎), going up to invade (עָלָה‎), being angry (אַף חָרָה אָנַף, הִתְעַבֵּר,‎), sinning or acting treacherously (כִּחֵשׁ כִּזֵּב, שִׁקֵּר, מָּשַׁע, מָעַל, מָרָה, מָרַד, בָּגַד, חָטָא,‎), testifying (הֵעִיד עָנָה,‎), mocking (הֵתֵל הִלְעִיג,‎), feeling loathing (קוּץ‎), rebuking (גָּעַר‎: properly to protest loudly), speaking (דִּבֶּר‎: Num 12:8b), etc., & even (an extreme case) Hosea 7:14 בִי יָסוּרוּ‎ they turn aside (so as to be) against me. In a weaker sense בַּקִּיר מַשְׁתִּין‎ mingens ad parietem 1Sam 25:22 and elsewhere

b. down to, upon (super with accusative), especially in such phrases as בּוֺ דָּמָיו‎ Lev 20:9 and elsewhere his blood be upon him; בְראֹשׁוֺ דָּמוֺ‎ his blood be upon his head Josh 2:19; י (הֵשִׁיב בְּראֹשׁוֺ׳שׁוּב )‎ Judges 8:57 (רָעָה‎), 1Kin 2:33 (דָּם‎), 2:44 (רָעָה‎), Psa 7:17 (עֲמָלוֺ‎); מּ דֶּרֶךְ נָתַן ׳בְּראֹשׁוֺ‎ 1Kin 8:32 & often in Ezekiel, as Ezek 9:10; 11:21.

III. 1. With —

a. of accompaniment: Num 20:20 כָּבֵד בְּעַם‎ with much people, Josh 22:8; Judg 11:34; 1Kin 10:2; 2Kin 5:9; Jer 41:15; Exod 21:22 and he shall give בִּפְלִלִים‎ with arbitrators (arbitrators being employed), Isa 8:16 בְּלִמֻּדָֽי׃‎ with my disciples, i.e. having them present; Exod 8:1; 8:13; Jer 11:19 בְּלַחְמוֺ עֵץ‎ a tree with its sap; 1Kin 19:19 הֶעָשָׂר בִּשְׁנֵים וְהוּא‎ and he with the 12th.

b. often of what one takes or brings with one: Gen 32:11 בְּמַקְלִי‎ with my staff I passed over Jordan, Judg 11:34; 15:1; 1Sam 1:24; Isa 7:24; Micah 6:6 and elsewhere בְּ קִדֵּם‎ to go to meet with; בְּ בָּא‎ to come with Lev 16:3; Psa 66:13; 71:16. (In Arabic this usage is developed more fully than in Hebrew, and literally to come with, literally to go away with, are used idiomatically in the sense of to bring, and to take away respectively: WAG ii. § 56 b.) Hence בְּלֹא בִּבְלִי, בְּאֶפֶס, בְּאֵין,‎ = without.

c. of concomitant (or surrounding) conditions, as בְּחִמָּזוֺן‎ with (or in) haste; בְּצֶדֶק‎ with (or in) righteousness; בִּשְׁגָגָה‎ in error; שׁוֺפָר וּבְקוֺל בִּתְרוּעָה‎ 2Sam 6:15; often in such phrases as בְּצִדְקָֽתְךָ‎ Psa 31:2 in thy righteousness; בְּחַסְדְּךָ‎ in thy mercy Exod 15:13; — בְּאָשְׁרִי‎ with my happiness! = happy am I Gen 30:13; Psa 29:4 the voice of ׳י‎ is בַּכֹּחַ‎ with power = is powerful; Exod 32:12 בְּרָעָה‎ with evil purpose; Psa 73:8 בְרָע‎ in wickedness; 90:10 בִּגְבוּרֹת‎ with strength.

2 of the instrument or means: as

a. בַּחֶרֶב‎ with the sword Exod 5:3 etc.; בְּרַגְלַיִם‎ with the feet Isa 28:3; . . . בְּיַד‎ by the hand of ... (see below יָד‎); to stone בְּאֶבֶן‎ or בָּֽאֲבָנִים‎ with stones Lev 20:2; Num 14:10 etc.; בְּ שָׁתָה‎ to drink with a cup Gen 44:5; Amos 6:6 (compare in Aramaic Dan 5:2); to cry בְּגָרוֺן‎ with the throat Isa 58:1; to burn בָּאֵשׁ‎ in or with fire (often); to slay or to perish בָּרָעָב‎ through hunger or בַּדֶּבֶר‎ through pestilence Exod 16:3; Jer 21:9 + often (compare Job 27:15 יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ בַּמָּוֶת‎); to save with or by Judg 7:7; 1Sam 14:6.

b. idiomatic, with certain verbs, as בְּ שָׁחַק‎ to play with Job 40:29; בְּ עָבַד‎ to labour with a person (as with an instrument), i.e. to use him as a slave Exod 1:14; Jer 22:13; 27:7 and elsewhere; בְּ עָשָׂה‎ 18:23; Neh 9:24; Dan 11:7; Est 1:15; 2:11; 3:11; 6:6; & perhaps בְּ דִּבֶּר‎ (of God) to speak with one Num 12:2, 8a and elsewhere (see Ew§ 217 f. (3); DrSm ii. 23, 2). Further ביהוה הִתְנַבֵּא בַּבַּעַל,‎ to prophesy with or by ׳י‎ or Baal, ׳י‎ or Baal being the inspirer; דָּרַשׁ בְּ, שָׁאַל‎ to inquire or ask by means of a god (or oracle).

c. ביהוה‎ through ׳י‎ (= by His aid) in many connections, as Psa 18:30; 44:6; 56:5; 56:11; Psalm 60:14; Isa 26:13; 45:25; Hosea 1:7; Zech 10:12; with passive verbs Deut 33:29; Isa 45:17 (to be saved): and even of the immediate cause Num 36:2 to be commanded ביהוה‎ by ׳י‎, Gen 9:6 בָּאָדָם‎ by man shall his blood be shed (both unusual), Hosea 14:4.

d. allied is the use of בְּ‎ in such phrases as to bless, swear, speak, prophesy, etc., בְּשֵׁם‎ in the name of ... (i.e. the name being used or appealed to in the act) Deut 6:13; Jer 11:21, etc. (so to swear ביהוה‎ by ׳י‎ Josh 2:12 etc.,בִּימִינוֺ‎ Isa 62:8; to bless בְּךָ‎ with thee Gen 48:20, to swear with me Psa 102:9, i.e. using my name in oath, Jer 29:22); almost = in the authority and power of 1Sam 17:45; 25:5; 1Kin 21:8; Micah 4:5; Zech 10:12; Psa 20:6; 44:6; 89:25.

e. בַּמָּה‎ or בַּמֶּה‎ by means of what? how? Gen 15:8; Judg 6:15; 16:5-6, 10; 1Kin 22:21; Mal 2:17. בְּזֹאת‎ by means of this Gen 42:15, 33. Exod 7:17; Num 16:28; with this = on this condition Gen 34:15, 22; 1Sam 11:2; Isa 27:9.

3 of cost or price (the Beth pretii), the price, whether given or received, being treated as the instrumental means by which the act is accomplished, with, for, at the cost of: thus regularly

a. with שָׂכַר‎ hire Gen 30:16, מָּדָה‎ redeem Exod 34:20, אֵרֵשׂ‎ betroth 2Sam 3:14, קָנָה‎ buy 24:24; 1Kin 2:23 בְּנַפְשׁוֺ‎ at the cost of his life hath A. spoken this word, 2Sam 23:17 who went בְּנַפְשׂוֺתָם‎ at peril of their lives, Prov 7:23; Lam 5:9; Josh 6:26 יְיַסְּדֶנָּה בִּבְכֹרוֺ‎ at the price of his firstborn shall he lay its foundations, 1Chr 12:19 בְּרָאשֵׁינוּ‎ to the jeopardy of our heads he will fall away, etc.

b. with מָכַר‎ sell Deut 21:14; עָבַד‎ serve Gen 29:18, 20; Hosea 12:13; הֵמִיר‎ exchange Lev 27:10; Hosea 4:7 their glory I will exchange for ignominy, Psa 106:20; בְּנֶשֶׁךְ נָתַן‎ to give for interest Lev 25:37; Psa 15:5; in other connections Gen 23:9; 47:16f.; Isa 45:13; Lam 1:11; Cant 8:7; 8:11; Deut 19:21 בְּעַיִן עַיִן בְּנֶפֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ‎ life for life, eye for eye; Isa 2:22 הוּא נֶחְשָׁב בַּמֶּה‎ at what is he to be accounted? 7:23 a thousand vines כָּ֑סֶף בְּאֶלֶף‎ at a thousand (shekels of) silver. — Hence (perhaps) the idiomatic usages בְשָׁנָה שָׁנָה‎ year for year, one year like another, annually Deut 15:20 and elsewhere; בְּיוֺם יוֺם‎ (late), בְּיוֺם כְּיוֺם‎ 1Sam 18:10; בְּפַעַם כְּפַעַם‎ (see מַּעַם יוֺם,‎); בְּחֹדֶשׁ חֹדֶשׁ‎ 1Chr 27:1.

4 rather peculiarly, in certain cases where the object of an action may be treated as the instrument by which it is accomplished: as בְּראֹשׁ הֵנַיעַ‎ to shake with the head Jer 18:6; Job 16:4 (as well as ראֹשׁ הֵנִיעַ‎ Psa 22:8); to open with the mouth Job 16:10, with the lips Psa 22:8; to gnash with the teeth Job 16:9 (to gnash the teeth Psa 35:16); to wink with the eye Prov 6:13 (to wink the eye, ib. 10:10); בְּקוֺל נָתַן‎ to utter with the voice Psa 46:7; 68:34; Jer 12:8 (but קוֺל נָתַן‎ is more common); to stretch out with the hand Lam 1:17; בַּמַּטֶּה הֵרִים‎ (unusual) Exod 7:20. So בְּשֵׁם קָרָא‎ to call with the name — in different senses, according to the context, namely, to proclaim 33:19; 34:5; Isa 44:5; Psa 49:12; to invoke Gen 4:26; 12:8; 1Kin 18:24-26 Isa 12:4; to name honourably 43:1; 45:3. compare Ew§ 282 d Ges§ 119. 3 b R. WAG ii. § 56 b β DeJob 31:12; Prov 20:30.

5 with a causal force, through, on account of: Gen 18:28 בַּחֲמִשָּׁה הֲתַשְׁחִית‎ wilt thou destroy on account of five the whole city? Lev 26:39; Num 16:26; Deut 9:4-5, 24:16 יוּמָֽתוּ׃ בְּחֶטְאוֺ אִישׁ‎ they shall be put to death, each because of his own sin (compare Jer 31:30; Ezek 3:18, see 18:17) 2Sam 3:27; 14:7 (compare Jonah 1:14) Isa 7:4 (|| מִן‎) 28:7 (|| מִן‎) 50:1; 53:5; 57:17; Jer 51:46; Psa 5:8; 5:11; 6:8 (|| מִן‎) 31:10; 32:3; 42:10; 90:9; 94:23. So in בִּגְלַל בַּאֲשֶׁר,‎ (see גָּלָל אֲשֶׁר,‎), & (sometimes) in בִּדְבַר‎ at, through, the word of ....

6 of the material with which a work is wrought, both absolute בַזָּהָב עָשָׁה‎ to work with gold Exod 31:4; 1Kin 7:14; and to make a thing with (in our idiom, of) gold Exod 38:8; Ezek 7:20; 1Kin 15:22 (בָּנָה‎). Without a verb Lev 13:52; 2Chr 9:18.

7 with for although, in spite of (compare German bei alle dem): Lev 26:27; Num 14:11 הָאֹתוֺת בְּכֹל‎ in spite of all the signs that I have wrought, Deut 1:32; Isa 47:9; Psa 27:3; especially in the phrase בְּכָלזֿאת‎ for all this Isa 5:25; 9:11; 9:16; 9:20; 10:4; Psa 78:32 and elsewhere (compare in Arabic Qor 9:25.)

8 of a standard of measurement or computation, with, by: Exod 12:4 נְפָשֹׁת בְּמִכְסַת‎ by the computation of souls; Leviticus 5:25 and elsewhere בְּעֶרְכְּךָ‎ by thy reckoning; Ezek 4:10; בְּמִסְמָּר‎ by number Deut 25:2 +; . . . בְּמִסְמַּר‎ by the number of ... Lev 25:15, 50; Num 1:2, etc.; הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּשֶׁקֶל‎ Exod 30:13 and elsewhere (in P); בָּאַמָּה‎ often (see אַמָּה‎); Deut 3:11 אִישׁ בְּאַמַּת‎ by the cubit of a man; 2Sam 14:26 הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּאֶבֶן‎. Of a model, Gen 1:26 בְּצַלְמֵנוּ‎ in our image, 5:1, 3; Exod 25:40; בְּדֶרֶךְ‎ with the way (= in the manner) of ... Isa 10:24, 26; Amos 4:10.

IV. בְּ‎ is used also with certain classes of verbs, though the explanation of its use may be sometimes doubtful: namely

a. with verbs of taking refuge, trusting, relying, as נִשְׁעַן חָסָה, בָּטַח, הֶאֱמִין,‎.

b. with verbs of ruling, governing, restraining, as שָׁלַט רָדָה, עָצַר, נָגַשׂ, מָשַׁל, מָלַךְ,‎.

c. with verbs of rejoicing, feeling pleasure or satisfaction, etc., as שָׂבַע רָצָה, חָפֵץ, שָׂמֵחַ, שׂוּשׂ, עָלַץ, גִּיל,‎ (but with this verb מִן‎ is more common). [Probably a case of

III. 5.]

d. with verbs expressive of sensible perception, to denote the pleasurable or attentive exercise of the faculty concerned, as בְּ שָׁמַע‎ to listen to, חָזָה רָאָה, בְּ, הִבִּיט‎, to look upon, בְּ הֵרִיחַ‎ to smell at (see these words).

e. occasionally also with verbs of speaking, thinking, mentioning, knowing, to denote the object of the action, as בְּ דִּבֶּר‎ to speak about Deut 6:7; Psa 87:3 and elsewhere (see below דִּבֶּר‎); שִׂיחַ הָגָה, בְּ, הִלֵּל‎ 44:9; 63:7; 69:13; יָדַע‎ Jer 38:24; זָכַר‎ once 3:16, הִזְכִּיר‎ often; Psa 71:6 תְהִלָּתִי בְּךָ‎ of thee is my praise.

V. Followed by an infinitive with, בְּ‎ forms a periphrasis for the gerund, though in English it is commonly to be rendered by a verb and conjunction, namely: —

1 as a temporal conjunction, as Gen 2:4 בְּהִבָּֽרְאָם‎ in their being created = when they were created, 4:8 בִּהְיוֺתָם‎ in their being (= when they were) in the field; and constantly. Sometimes it has in appearance the force of after that, as 33:18; Exod 3:12; 13:17; but as a rule this is really due to the action denoted by the infinitive being treated as extending over a period within which the action of the principal verb takes place: so especially in the phrase מִמִּצְרַיִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּצֵאת‎, even of events at the close of the 40 years, Deut 4:45; 23:5; Josh 5:4, the whole period being treated as that in which Egypt was left (compare 2Kin 2:1, where the time included is future). Cases, however, occur in which this explanation will hardly apply, as Deut 27:4; 24:12.

2 as a causal conjunction (compare above

III. 5), as Gen 19:16 עָלָיו י ׳בְּחֶמְלַת‎ through J.'s having compassion upon him, Exod 16:7; 33:16; 34:29; Deut 1:27 י ׳בְּשִׂנְאַת אֹתָנוּ‎ through J.'s hating us, etc. (9:28 similarly מִן‎), 1Kin 18:18 (= in that ye have ...) Ezek 9:8; 43:8; 44:7; 2Chr 28:6.

3 as a concessive conjunction, when = though: Isa 1:15; Psa 46:3 אָ֑רֶץ בְּהָמִיר‎ though the earth do change.

g. = expanse of country, opposed to mountain, in phrase שׂ ׳מְרוֺמֵי‎ Judg 5:18; בַּשּׂ ׳הֲרָרִי‎ Jer 17:3 (of Jerusalem) is dubious; compare הַשּׂ ׳לְעִי‎ Micah 1:6 (Jer 18:14 see שָׂדַי‎).

a. cultivated ground Gen 37:7 (E), 47:24 (J; הַשָּׂדֶה זֶרַע‎), Exod 22:4 (3 t. in verse); 22:5 (E), Lev 27:16-17, (P), Micah 3:12 (in simile) Ruth 2:2 47t., + תְרוּמוֺת שְׂדֵי‎ 2Sam 1:21, זָֿ֑רַע׳שׂ‎ Ezek 17:5, טוֺב שָׂדֶה‎ V:8 good soil.

of a territory Canaan (ᵐ5‎ Ξανααν, Phoenician כנען‎ = Phoenicia; Ξνα = כנע‎, Hecataeus, see MüllerFr.Hist.Gr.i,17 and others; Egyptian Ka-n-±-na WMMAs.u.Europa,205 ff.; Tel Amarna Kina—na, Kina——i, etc., BezBM Tablets, 150 WklTA 39; etymology dubious GFMPAOS Oct. 1890. lxvii ff.; see also GASmGeogr. 4 f. כְּנַעֲנָה‎ proper name, masculine 1. father of prophet Zedekiah 1Kin 22:11, 24 2Chr 18:10, 23 (ᵐ5‎ Ξανααν, Ξαανα, Ξανανα).

2 a Benjamite 1Chr 7:10 (ᵐ5‎ Ξανααν, Ξαναναν).

כנף‎ √ of following (meaning dubious; Arabic fence in, enclose, and Aramaic כְּנַף‎ collect, assemble, are denominative)

כנעני.def:
H3669. Kna

'aniy I. כְּנַעֲנִי‎ adjective and

name, of a people of I. כְּנַעַן‎; — usually masculine singular (הַ)כְּנַעֲנִי‎ Gen 38:2; Num 21:1 +; feminine singular הַכְּנַעֲנִית‎ Gen 46:10 = Exod 6:15; 1Chr 2:3 masculine plural (הַ)כְּנַעֲנִים‎ Obadiah 20; Neh 9:24; — 1. adjective כ ׳אִישׁ‎ Gen 38:2 (J). 2 with article as

substantive, a. of individual, ׳מֶלֶךְעֲֿרָדהַכּ‎ Num 21:1 (J) and hence 33:40 (P or R); feminine הַכְּנַעֲנִיתּ‎ Gen 46:10 = Exod 6:15 (P) הַכְּנַעֲנִית בַּתשֿׁוּעַ‎ 1Chr 2:3.

b. usually collective (with article) of pre-Israel in-habitants of כְּנַעַן‎ (q. v.) Gen 12:6; 24:3, 37; 50:11 (all J), Num 21:3 (J), Josh 13:3 (D), Judg 1:1, 3, 9, 10, 17, many of whom continued to live in the midst of Israel, 1:27; 1:28; 1:29; 1:29; 1:30; 1:32; 1:33; Josh 16:10 (twice in verse); 17:12-13, 16, 18 (all J E), 1Kin 9:16; plural only Obadiah 20, and הַכְּנַעֲנִים הָאָרֶץ ישְׁבֵי‎ Neh 9:24; הַכּ ׳מִשְׁמְּחוֺת‎ Gen 10:18, הַכּ ׳גְּבוּל‎ 10:19 (both J), הַכּ ׳אֶרֶץ‎ Exod 13:11 (JE), Ezek 16:3; often of part of the inhabitants, ׳הַכּ הָאָרֶץ ישְׁבֵי וְכָל‎ Josh 7:9 (JE), Deut 11:30; with other proper name, of a people, + הַמְּרִזִּי‎ Gen 13:7; 34:30 (both J), Judg 1:4-5, + הָאֱמֹרִי‎ Deut 1:7; Josh 5:1; 13:4 (all D); + הַחִוִּי‎ 2Sam 24:7; + (יׅ עֲמָלֵקִ‎ Num 14:25, 43, 45; especially in the list of peoples dispossessed by Israel, Gen 15:21; Exod 3:8, 17; 13:5; 23:23, 28; 33:2; 34:11; Num 13:29 (׳הַכּ‎ dwelling by the sea and along Jordan [compare Deut 1:7; 11:30; Josh 5:1; 11:3; 13:4]; all these J E), Deut 7:1; 20:17; Josh 3:10; 9:1; 11:3; 12:8; 24:11 (all J E D), Judg 3:3, 5; hence Ezra 9:1; Neh 9:8. compare DrDt. p. 11, 13 f., 97, 133.

II. כְּנַעֲנִי‎ noun masculine trader, merchant (compare II. כְּנַעַן‎); only singular (but see below): — י כ׳בְּבֵית יִהְיֶה ׳וְלֹא עוֺד‎ Zech 14:21 (probably); לַכּ נָָֽתְנָה ׳וַחֲגוֺר‎ Prov 31:24 (|| וַתִּמְכֹּר עָֽשְׂתָה סָדִין‎). **plural suffix כִּנְעָנֶיהָ‎ (si vera lectio) Isa 23:8 (|| סֹחֲרֶיהָ‎). In Zech 11:7, 11 read perhaps (לִ)כְנַעֲנִיֵּי‎ for ᵐ5 עֲנִיֵּי, (לָ)כֵן‎ Ξαναναῖοι, Ξαναανῖτιν, StaZAW, 1881. 26 (who compare as to sense Hosea 12:8), compare Klo We Marti.

H3670. kanaph

[כָּנַף‎] verb denominative from כָּנָף‎ 2 only

כנרת.def:
H3672. Kinaroth

or Kinnereth ִכּנְַֿרוֺת כִּנֶּ֫רֶתֵ,‎ proper name, of a location in Galilee (Naphtali), כִּנֶּרֶת‎ Deut 3:17; Josh 13:27; Num 34:11; כִּנָּ֑רֶת‎ Josh 19:35; ִכּנְַֿרוֺת‎ (so Baer; ִכּנְרוֺת‎ Norzi) 11:2; 12:3; 1Kin 15:20; —

2 יָםכִּֿנֶּרֶת‎, lake near the city, Num 34:11 (P; ᵐ5‎ B Ξεναρα, A Ξενερεθ), Josh 13:27 (P; ᵐ5‎ B Ξενερεθ; A ᵐ5‎L Ξενερωθ), ִכּנְַֿרוֺת יָם‎ 12:3 (D; ᵐ5‎ B Ξενερεθ; A Ξεννερεθ); כָּלִֿכּנְַֿרוֺת‎ 1Kin 15:20 +?πᾶσαν τὴνγῆν Ξενερεθ ᵐ5‎L, — ᵑ7‎ has גִּנֹּסַר גְּנֵיסַר, גִּינֵסַר,‎, compare τὸ ὕδωρ τοῦ Γεννησαρ1Makk. 1 Kings 11:67; Γεννησαρετ Mark 6:53; Matt 14:34; Luke 5:1; etymological connection with כִּנֶּרֶת‎ disputed by GASmGeogr. 443 n. כנש.def:
H3673. kenash

[כְּנַשׁ‎] verb gather (ᵑ7‎ id.; Old Aramaic Palmyrene בנש‎ Lzb298; Syriac ; see also Biblical Hebrew [כָּנַס‎); —

Pe`al Infinitive, לְמִכְנַשׁ‎, followed by ל‎ accusative of person Dan 3:2.

Hithpa. Participle plural מִתְכַּנְּשִׁין‎ (were) assembled Dan 3:3, 27.

כנת.def:
H3674. kenath

[כְּנָת‎] noun [of men, but feminine in form, Ges§ 122, 4. b] associate, colleague (loan-word from Biblical Aramaic כְּנָת‎; Syriac , compare also SchwIdioticon 46; on formative see LagBN 82); — only Aram plural כְּנָוֺתָו֯ שְׁאָר‎ Ezra 4:7 the rest of his associates.

כסא.def:
H430. elohim

אֱלֹהִים‎2570 noun masculine plural (feminine 1Kin 11:33; on number of occurrences of אֱלֹהִים אֱלוֺהַּ, אֵל,‎ compare also Nesl. c,)

a. rulers, judges, either as divine representatives at sacred places or as reflecting divine majesty and power: האלהים‎ Exod 21:6 (Onk ᵑ6‎, but τὸ κριτήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ ᵐ5‎) 22:7; 22:8; אלהים‎ 22:8; 22:27 (ᵑ7‎ Ra AE Ew RVm; but gods, ᵐ5‎ Josephus Philo AV; God, Di RV; all Covt. code of E) compare 1Sam 2:25 see Dr.; Judg 5:8 (Ew, but gods ᵐ5‎; God ᵑ6‎ BarHebr.; ᵑ9 יהוה‎ Be) Psa 82:1; 82:6 (De Ew Pe; but angels Bl Hup) 138:1 (ᵑ7 ᵑ6‎ Rab Ki De; but angels ᵐ5‎ Calv; God, Ew; gods, Hup Pe Che).

b. divine ones, superhuman beings including God and angels Psa 8:6 (De Che Br; but angels ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Ew; God, RV and most moderns) Gen 1:27 (if with Philo ᵑ7‎ Jerome De Che we interpret נעשה‎ as God's consultation with angels; compare Job 38:7).

c. angels Psalm Job 97:7 (ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Calv; but gods, Hup De Pe Che); compare (ה)אלהים בני‎ = (the) sons of God, or sons of gods = angels Job 1:6; 2:1; 38:7; Gen 6:2, 4 (J; so ᵐ5‎ Books of Enoch & Jubilees Philo Jude Judg 1:6 2Pet 2:4 JosAnt. i. 3. 1, most ancient fathers and modern critics; against usage are sons of princes, mighty men, Onk and Rab.; sons of God, the pious, Theod Chrys Jerome Augustine Luther Calv Hengst; ᵐ5‎L read οἱ υιὁὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ), compare אלים בני‎.

d. gods האלהים‎ Exod 18:11; 22:19 (E) 1Sam 4:8; 2Chr 2:4; Psa 86:8; האלהים אלהי‎ the God of gods, supreme God Deut 10:17; Psa 136:2; אלהים‎ Exod 32:1, 23 (JE) Judg 9:13; אחרים אלהים‎ other gods Exod 20:3; 23:13; Josh 24:2, 16 (E) Deut 31:18, 20 (JE) 5:7 + (17 t. in D, not P) Judg 2:12, 17, 19; 10:13; 1Sam 8:8; 26:19; 1Kin 9:6, 9 (= 2Chr 7:19, 22) 11:4, 10; 14:9; 2Kin 5:17; 17:35, 37, 38; 22:17 (= 2Chr 34:25) 28:25; Jer 1:16 + (18 t. a. god or goddess, always with suffix 1Sam 5:7 (Dagon), Judg 11:24 (Chemosh), 1Kin 18:24 (Baal), Judg 9:27; Dan 1:2 (twice in verse); or construct ׳א א לכמוש ׳צדנים מואב לעשתרת‎ to Ashtoreth goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh god of Moab, etc. 1Kin 11:33; ׳א הארץ‎ god of the land 2Kin 17:26 (twice in verse); 17:27, and so the Syrians suppose that Yahweh is a mountain-god and not a god of valleys 1Kin 20:28.

b. godlike one Exod 4:16 (J; Moses in relation to Aaron), 7:1 (P; in relation to Pharaoh), 1Sam 28:13 (the shade of Samuel), Psa 45:7 (the Messianic king, O God, ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Jerome, most scholars ancient and modern, but thy throne is God's = God's throne AE Ki Thea Ew Hup, compare 1Chr 28:5). c. works of God, or things specially belonging to him (see אֵל‎ 5) אלהים הר‎ Psa 68:16; Ezek 28:14, 16; אלהים אש‎ Job 1:16; (ה)אלהים גן‎ Ezek 28:13; 31:8-9,. d. God (see 3 & 4).

Qal, only Participle active כֹּסֶה‎; —

1 conceal shame Prov 12:16; knowledge 12:23.

2 passive (construct) חֲטָאָה כְּסוּי‎ Psa 32:1 covered in respect of sin (by God, which he thus puts out of sight) (|| נְשׂוּימֶּֿשַׁע‎).

Niph`al Perfect3feminine singular נִכְסָ֑תָּה‎, covered, with waves Jer 51:42; Infinitive construct הִכָּסוֺת‎ Ezek 24:8, (blood) not to be covered.

Pi`el Perfect3masculine singular כִּסָּה‎ Num 9:15 12t.; suffix כִּסָּהוּ‎ Lev 17:13; Num 17:7; כִּסָּמוֺ‎ Exod 15:10; 3feminine singular כִּסְּתָה‎ Gen 38:15 5t.; 1 singular כִּסִּיתִי‎ Psa 32:5 3t.; כִּסֵּתִי‎ Ezek 31:15 (strike out Co); כִּסֵּיתִי‎ 32:7 13t. Perfect; Imperfect3masculine singular יְכַסֶּה‎ Isa 6:2 8t.; וַיְכַס‎ Exod 10:15 4t.; suffix יְכַסֶּ֑דָּ‎ Hab 2:17; יְכַסֶּנָּה‎ Ezek 30:18; 3masculine plural suffix יְכַסְיֻמוּ‎ Exod 15:5 41t. Imperfect; Imperative suffix כַּסּוּנוּ‎ Hosea 10:8; Infinitive construct כַּסּוֺת‎ Mal 2:13 11t.; כַּסֹּת‎ Num 4:15; suffix כַּסֹּתוֺ‎ Exod 26:13; Participle מְכַסֶּה‎ Prov 10:18 12t.; plural מְכַסִּים‎ Isa 11:9; feminine plural מְכַסּוֺת‎ Ezek 1:11, 23 (twice in verse); —

1 cover, clothe Judg 4:19; Ezek 16:10 (2 accusative), 16:18; Jonah 3:6 is apparently reflexive, with accusative of garment (strange; read perhaps וַיִּכָּס‎); nakedness Gen 9:23 (J), Exod 28:42 (P), Ezek 16:8; Hosea 2:11; the naked Isa 58:7; Ezek 18:7, 16 (+ accusative of thing); the face and legs of seraphim Isa 6:2 (twice in verse); bodies of cherubim Ezek 1:11, 23 (twice in verse); the face Gen 38:15 (J), Ezek 12:6, 12, figurative Job 23:17; earth with the great deep Psa 104:6; heavens with glory Hab 3:3; with בְּ‎ of the clothing Gen 38:14 (J), Deut 22:12, these two apparently reflexive, compare Jonah 3:6 above; Judg 4:18; 1Kin 1:1; heaven with clouds Psa 147:8, with glory Ezek 32:7.

2 cover, conceal blood Gen 37:26 (J), Job 16:18; human ordure Deut 23:14; mountains conceal men from God Hosea 10:8; cover transgressions Job 31:33; Prov 17:9; 28:13; iniquity Psa 32:5; righteousness 40:11; hatred Prov 10:18; a thing 11:13; face of judge so that he cannot see justice Job 9:24; rulers and seers Isa 29:10; with בְּ‎ of covering Lev 17:13 (H), 1Sam 19:13; face by fat Job 15:27; sun by a cloud Ezek 32:7; with מִן‎ from whom Gen 18:17 (J), Job 33:17.

3 cover (with covering of protection), a pit Exod 21:33 (Covt. code); with cloud of incense, the Kapporeth Lev 16:13 (P); coverings of the sacred tent, tabernacle, and their furniture Exod 26:13; Num 4:9, 15 (P); with בְּ‎ of the covering 4:5, 8, 11, 12 (P); Zion יָדִי בְּצֵל‎ Isa 51:16.

4 cover, spread over, fat, the inwards Exod 29:13, 22; Lev 3:3, 9, 14; 4:8 (with עַל‎), 7:3 (P); leprosy, the skin and flesh 13:12-13, (P); the cloud of the theophany, the mount Exod 24:15-16, (P), the tent of meeting 40:34; Num 17:7 (P), and the tabernacle 9:15-16, (P); altar with tears Mal 2:13 (2 accusative); Jerusalem with multitude of camels Isa 60:6; of handiwork 1Kin 7:18, 41, 42 2Chr 4:12-13,.

5 cover, overwhelm, followed by accusative, the sea the Egyptians Exod 14:28 (P), 15:5, 10 (song), Josh 24:7 (E), Psa 78:53; 106:11; waters Job 22:11; 38:34; Psa 104:9; Jer 46:8; Ezek 26:19; locusts the eye of the land Exod 10:5, 15 (J), also Israel Num 22:5, 11 (J); frogs the land Exod 8:2 (P); quails the camp 16:13 (P); cloud the land Ezek 30:18; 38:9, 16; darkness the earth Isa 60:2; dust a city Ezek 26:10; the depths of the sea by God Job 36:30; with a reference to a person's shame Psa 44:16; 69:8; Jer 51:51; Obadiah 10; Micah 7:10; horror Psa 55:6; Ezek 7:18; violence Prov 10:6, 11; Hab 2:17; confusion Jer 3:25; mischief Psa 140:10; God covers sin 85:3 (|| עון נשׂא‎), compare 32:1 (Qal).

6 followed by על‎ of person or thing covered, cover over: cherubim over the ark 2Chr 5:8; over the dead, the earth Num 16:33 (JE), Psa 106:17; Isa 26:21, worms Job 21:26; dust over blood Ezek 24:7; waters over the sea Hab 2:14, compare לַיָּם‎ Isa 11:9; (see Dr§ 135. 7 Obs.); love covereth over all sins Prov 10:12; God covereth over iniquity Nehemiah 3:37; people not to cover over a guilty person Deut 13:9; + accusative of object covering (DaSynt. § 75), figurative covering over the garment with violence Mal 2:16; God's hands with light Job 36:32; + בְּ‎ of covering Psa 44:20.

Note. — כִסִּתִי אֵלֶיךָ) (‎ Psa 143:9 is error for חָסִיתִי‎ according to ᵐ5‎ κατέφυγον SS, but חסה‎ not construct with אֶלֿ‎; חִכִּיתִי‎ Bae; אֶתתְּֿהוֺם עָלָיו כִּסֵּתִי הֶאֱבַלְתִּי‎ Ezek 31:15 according to Co I caused the deep to mourn for them (strike out כסתי‎).

Pual. Perfect3masculine plural כָּסּוּ‎ Psa 80:11; Prov 24:31; Imperfect יְכֻסֶּה‎ Eccl 6:4; plural וַיְכֻסּוּ‎ Gen 7:19-20, Participle plural מְכֻסִּים‎ 1Chr 21:16; feminine plural מְכֻסּוֺת‎ Ezek 41:16.

1 followed by accusative be covered, hills with shadow Psa 80:11; mountains with water Gen 7:19-20, (P); field with nettles Prov 24:31; absolute, windows of temple Ezek 41:16.

2 followed by בְּ‎, be clothed, with sackcloth 1Chr 21:16; name with darkness Eccl 6:4.

Hithpa`el Imperfect וַיִּתְכַּס‎ Isa 37:1 = 2Kin 19:1; 3feminine singular תִּכַּסֶּה‎ Prov 26:26; וַתִּתְכָּ֑ס‎ Gen 24:65; plural יִתְכַּסּוּ‎ Isa 59:6; Jonah 3:8; Participle מִתְכַּסֶּה‎ 1Kin 11:29; plural מִתְכַּסִּים‎ Isa 37:2 = 2Kin 19:2; — cover, clothe oneself, absolute (of veil) Gen 24:65 (J); with בְּ‎, of new garment 1Kin 11:29; sackcloth 2Kin 19:1-2,= Isa 37:1-2, figurative of works 59:6, of hatred with guile Prov 26:26; with accusative Jonah 3:5 (שַׂקִּים‎).

כסוי.def:
H3681. kasuy

[כָּסוּי‎] noun [masculine] covering, only construct עוֺר כְּסוּי‎ covering of skins Num 4:6, 14 (P).

כסולת.def:
H3694. Kesulloth

כְּסֻלּוֺת‎ proper name, of a location in the tribe of Issachar Josh 19:18, = תָּבֹר כִּסְלֹת‎ (loins or flanks of Tabor), on the western foot of Mt. Tabor, 19:12; = תָּבוֺר‎ 19:22; 1Chr 6:62; = modern Iksâl RobBR iii. 182, Memi. 365 BuhlG. § 113, p. 216.

כסות.def:
H3682. kesuth

כְּסוּת‎ noun feminine covering — ׳כ‎ Gen 20:16 3t.; suffix כְּסוּתְךָ‎ Deut 22:12 3t. suffixes; —

1 covering, clothing Exod 21:10; 22:26 (Covt. code), Deut 22:12; Job 24:7; 31:19; of שַׂק‎ as clothing of heavens Isa 50:3 in figure

2 covering for concealment, of Abaddon, the subterranean abode of the dead Job 26:6; ׳כ עֵינַיִם‎, covering of the eyes Gen 20:16 (so that they cannot see the wrong, figurative of a present offered in compensation for it; E).

כסח.def:
H3683. kasach

[כָּסַח‎] verb cut off or away, a plant (Late Hebrew id.; Aramaic כְּסַח‎, (for Hebrew זָמַר‎); Arabic sweep off, away, destroy, do away with; compare Sabean כסח‎ overpower, conquer, HomZMG 1892, 532) — only

Qal Passive participle, feminine singular כְּסוּחָה‎ Psa 80:17, cut away, of Israel under figure of vine; masculine plural כְּסוּחִים קוֺצִים‎ Isa 33:12 thorns cut away, figurative of peoples destroyed by divine judgment.

כסיל.def:
H3686. Kesil

III. כְּסִיל‎ proper name, of a location in south of tribe of Judah Josh 15:30, probably corrupt for בְּתוּל‎ 19:4; see בְּתוּאֵל‎.

כסילות.def:
H3687. kesiluth

כְּסִילוּת‎ noun feminine stupidity; — Prov 9:13 כ ׳אֵשֶׁת‎, the woman Stupidity, in antithesis with חָכְמוֺת‎ the Supreme Wisdom personified as a woman.

כסל.def:
H3688. kasal

[כָסַל‎] verb be or become stupid (Late Hebrew Aramaic in derivatives; Arabic be sluggish, so North Syriac in derivatives; original meaning possibly thick, plump, fat; hence in good sense: כְּסָלִים‎ loins, כִּסְלָה כֶּסֶל,‎ confidence; in bad sense: כְּסִילוּת כִּסְלָה, כֶּסֶל,‎ stupidity, folly, כְּסִיל‎ stupid fellow) —

Qal Imperfect יִכְסָ֑לוּ‎ they become stupid Jer 10:8 (|| יִבְעֲרוּ‎ they become brutish).

כסלו.def:
H3691. Kislev

כִּסְלֵו‎ proper name [masculine] kislew, ninth month (post-exilic) = November-December, Zech 7:1; כ ׳בְּחֹדֶשׁ‎ Neh 1:1 (ᵑ7‎ id.; loan-word from Babylonian kislimu, kislivu, Muss-ArnJBL 1892, 167; conjectures on etymology by JenZA ii, 210, Anm. 3 Hptib. 265, Anm. 2; Palmyrene כסלול‎ VogNo. 24; Greek χασελευ I Makk Nehemiah 1:54).

כסלון.def:
H3693. Kesalon

כְּסָלוֺן‎ proper name, of a location on border of tribe of Judah = הַריְֿעָרִים‎ Josh 15:10; = Kesla10miles west of Jerusalem, GuérinJud. ii. 11 ff. Memiii. 25. 26 BuhlG. § 92, p. 166.

כסלחים.def:
H3695. Kasluchim

כַּסְלֻחִים‎ proper name, of a people Gen 10:14 (ᵐ5‎ D Ξασμωνιειμ, ᵐ5‎L Ξασλωνιειμ E Ξαλοειμ) = 1Chr 1:12 (A Ξασλωνιειμ, ᵐ5‎L Ξασλωειμ), among the sons of מִָצְרַיִם‎ not identified; conjectures in Thes Di.

תָּבוֺר כִּסְלֹת‎ see כְּסֻלּוֺת‎ above

כסם.def:
H3697. kasam

[כָּסַם‎] verb shear, clip (Assyrian kasâmu, cut in pieces, according to DlHWB 344); — only

Qal Imperfect and Infinitive absolute אֶתרָֿאשֵׁיהֶם יִכְסְמוּ כָּסוֺם‎ Ezek 44:20 they shall by all means clip their heads (opposed to יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ‎ shave and יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ‎, i.e. let grow freely).

כסמים.def:
H3698. kussemeth

כֻּסֶּ֫מֶת‎ noun feminine spelt, triticum spelta (Late Hebrew plural כוּסְמִין‎, compare כונתא ᵑ6 ᵑ7‎, ; compare Löwp. 104 ff. DiExod 9:23 NowArch i, 111); — absolute ׳כ‎ 9:32; Isa 28:25 plural כֻּסְּמִים‎ Ezek 4:9 (in all distinguished from wheat, barley, etc.)

כסמת.def:
H3698. kussemeth

כֻּסֶּ֫מֶת‎ noun feminine spelt, triticum spelta (Late Hebrew plural כוּסְמִין‎, compare כונתא ᵑ6 ᵑ7‎, ; compare Löwp. 104 ff. DiExod 9:23 NowArch i, 111); — absolute ׳כ‎ 9:32; Isa 28:25 plural כֻּסְּמִים‎ Ezek 4:9 (in all distinguished from wheat, barley, etc.)

כסס.def:
H3699. kasas

[כָּסַס‎] verb compute (perhaps originally divide up, make small, fine; Late Hebrew chew; Aramaic break small (rare), usually (Aph`el etc.) correct, convict; Arabic pulverize; Assyrian kasâsu, perhaps cut in two, or up, whence kissatu, fodder) — only

Qal Imperfect2masculine plural עַלהַֿשֶּׂה תָּכֹסּוּ אָכְלוֺ לְפִי אִישׁ‎ Exod 12:4 (P) each one according to his eating shall ye compute for the lamb.

כסף.def:
H3702. kesaph

כְּסַף‎ noun masculineEzra 7:17 silver (see Biblical Hebrew); — absolute ׳כ‎ 7:15 +, כְּסַ֑ף‎ Dan 2:32; emphatic כַּסְמָּא‎ 2:35 +; —

1 as material Dan 2:32, 35, 45; Ezra 5:14; 6:5.

2 as money or its equivalent Ezra 7:17, 7:15; 7:16; 7:18; 7:22.

כְּעֶת כְּעֶ֫נֶת, כְּעַן,‎ see below ענה‎.

כספיא.def:
H3703. Kasiphya

כָּסִפְיָא‎ proper name, of a location in Babylonia, site un-known: — ׳בְּכ הַמָּקוֺם‎ Ezra 8:17 (twice in verse) ᵐ5‎ B ἐν ἀργυρίῳ, ᵐ5‎L ἐν Μασφεν Esdr a, τῶν γαζοφυλακίων, γαζοφύλαξιν Esdr β.

כֶּסֶת‎ see below II. כסה‎.

כסת.def:
H3704. keseth

[כֶּ֫סֶת‎] noun feminine band, fillet (= charm or amulet according to Ehpraimitic source Syriac, φυλακτήρια according to ὁ Ἑβραῖος of Hexapl., compare RSJPh xiii, 286; in Late Hebrew כסת‎ usually = cushion, bolster, pillow), only plural עַלֿ כְּסָתוֺת מְתַמְּרוֺת‎ Ezek 13:18 women sewing bands upon elbows; with suffix 2 feminine plural כִּסְתוֺתֵיכֶ֫נָה‎ 13:20.

כֶּסֶה‎ see כֶּסֶא‎.

כִּסֵּה‎ see כִּסֵּא‎.

כען.def:
H3705. kean

כְּעַן‎ adverb now (so Egyptian Aramaic (CISii. 137 = CookeNo.73 RÉS:361 B S-CPap. C 5); ᵑ7‎, e.g. Num 22:4: עַן‎ probably a substantive from [עָנָה‎] the √ of עֵת‎, time; so כְּעַן‎ literally at (this) time = Hebrew עַתָּה‎: K§ 67, 4); — Dan 2:23 הוֺדַעְתַּנִי וּכְעַן‎, 3:15; 4:34; 5:12, 15, 16; 6:9; Ezra 4:13-14, 21; 5:17; 6:6; עַדכְּֿעַן‎ until now 5:16 (so ᵑ7‎ Gen 18:22 +).

כענת.def:
H3706. keeneth

or keeth כְּעֶ֫נֶת‎ and (Ezra 4:17) contracted כְּעֶת‎ adverb now (feminine of כְּעַן‎; so first SS TorreyJBL 16 (1897), 166 ff.; now confirmed by Egyptian Aramaic כענת‎ CowleyPSBA xxv. 264, 311, 312 ( = RES492-4 = S-CM, N, O); ׳וכ‎ formerly taken to mean and so forth); — always ׳וּכ‎, and always in a letter, introducing the business of the letter, and to be connected with what follows, not, as ᵑ0‎, with what precedes: 4:10 (strike out, as introduced by error from end of 4:11), 4:11 (joining to 4:12) and now, let it be known, etc., 4:17f. and now, the letter which, etc., 7:12f. and now, I make a decree, etc. (compare וְעַתָּה‎ similarly in letters 2Kin 5:6; 10:2, and καὶ νῦν2Macc 1:6).

כעס.def:
H3708. ka

'ac כַּ֫עַס‎ noun masculine vexation, anger; — ׳כ‎ Deut 32:27 13t.; כָּ֑עַס‎ Prov 21:19; Eccl 1:18; suffix כַּעְסִי‎ 1Sam 1:16, כַּעַסְךָ‎ Psa 85:5, כַּעְסוֺ‎ Prov 12:16; 1Kin 15:30; plural כְּעָסִים‎ 2Kin 23:26. — vexation:

1 of men, especially caused by unmerited treatment, 1Sam 1:6, 16; Prov 12:16; 17:25; 21:19; 27:3; Eccl 7:9.

2 vexation, anger of Yahweh (caused especially by worship of other gods) 1Kin 15:30; 21:22; 2Kin 23:26; ׳כ עִמָּנוּ‎ Psa 85:5 anger (of Yahweh) with us; ׳כ בָּנָיו‎ Deut 32:19 anger against his sons, ׳כ אוֺיֵב‎ 32:27 anger against the enemy (both object Genitive see Di; RV provocation of, compare Dr); ׳כ קָרְבָּנָם‎ Ezek 20:28 provocation of their offering (so RV but Co strike out, rightly).

3 vexation, grief Psa 6:8; 10:14; 31:10; Eccl 1:18; 2:23; 7:3; 11:10, also כעס‎ 5:16 accusative Ew aI.

כַּ֫עַשׂ‎ noun masculine (dialectic variation of כַּעַם‎, only in Job); — ׳כ‎ Job 17:7, כָּ֑עָשׂ‎ 5:2; suffix כַּעְשִׂי‎ 6:2; כַּעַשְׂךָ‎ 10:17; —

1 vexation, grief of men Job 5:2 (compare Prov 12:16; 27:3), 6:2; 17:7.

2 vexation, anger, of God; with עִמָּדִי כַּעַשְׂךָ‎ Job 10:17 thine anger with me.

כַּף‎ see below כפף‎.

כעת.def:
H3706. keeneth

or keeth כְּעֶ֫נֶת‎ and (Ezra 4:17) contracted כְּעֶת‎ adverb now (feminine of כְּעַן‎; so first SS TorreyJBL 16 (1897), 166 ff.; now confirmed by Egyptian Aramaic כענת‎ CowleyPSBA xxv. 264, 311, 312 ( = RES492-4 = S-CM, N, O); ׳וכ‎ formerly taken to mean and so forth); — always ׳וּכ‎, and always in a letter, introducing the business of the letter, and to be connected with what follows, not, as ᵑ0‎, with what precedes: 4:10 (strike out, as introduced by error from end of 4:11), 4:11 (joining to 4:12) and now, let it be known, etc., 4:17f. and now, the letter which, etc., 7:12f. and now, I make a decree, etc. (compare וְעַתָּה‎ similarly in letters 2Kin 5:6; 10:2, and καὶ νῦν2Macc 1:6).

כף.def:
H3710. keph

[כֵּף‎] noun [masculine] rock (Assyrian kâpu DlHWB 346; Aramaic כֵּיפָא‎, perhaps Aramaic loan-word in Hebrew; √ dubious); — only plural כֵּפִים‎ Jer 4:29 as place of refuge; Job 30:6 as dwelling-place.

כפה.def:
H3711. kaphah

[כָּפָה‎] verb probably subdue (Late Hebrew overturn, hold under, compel; Aramaic כְּפָא‎, id.; incline (as face to ground), overturn; Assyrian kipû perhaps id., DlHWB 346; compare Arabic overturn, turn back); — only

Qal Imperfect יִכְמֶּהאָֿ֑ף בַּסֵּתֶר מַתָּן‎ Prov 21:14 a gift in secret subdueth anger (so Thes Rob-Ges; Ew beugt: Fl De averteth, from the Arabic, is more remote; ᵐ5‎ ἀνατρέπει, compare Late Hebrew).

כִּמָּה‎ see below כפף‎.

כפור.def:
H3713. kphowr

I. כְּפוֺר‎ noun masculine bowl (Late Hebrew id.; ᵑ7‎. כְּפוֺרָא‎) — bowl of gold or sliver, used in the temple (late), ׳כ‎ 1Chr 28:17 (4 t. in verse); plural construct כְּפוֺרֵי‎ 28:17 (twice in verse); Ezra 1:10 (twice in verse); 8:27.

II. כְּפוֺר‎ noun masculine hoar frost (Late Hebrew id.) — ׳כ‎ Psa 147:16; כְּפֹר‎ Exod 16:14 (P), Job 38:29.

כפיס.def:
H3714. kaphis

כָּפִיס‎ noun masculine apparently (si vera lectio) technical term for some beam in a house, perhaps rafter, or girder (Late Hebrew id., Levy, Jastrow, but according to HoffmZAW ii. 1881, 71 it is changed from oblong block of wood (O.T.) to a building-stone, or brick in Mishna); — only Hab 2:11 for a stone out of the wall crieth out, ׳וְכ יַעֲנֶנָּה מֵעֵץ‎ and a rafter out of the timber-work answereth it.

כפיר.def:
